subject: Android Leads update - L team follow-up
excerpt: Sundar was supportive and confirmed he would discuss with L-team next Monday. His other feedback was that i) we should not pro-actively amend existing MADA's; adjusting language at renewal is fine, and ii) he'd like to soften the MADA to make it more gentle. We also discussed that the OEM search revenue share deals is a good place to re-insert this kind of language/commitment.
context: A Google Android partnerships lead reports Sundar Pichai's view on search-default language in the phone maker contract.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0616, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: [Samsung Sidewinder] Quick question about placement discussion in global MADA
excerpt: let me state it more stringently. The widget and Play Store icon are staying. And there is a 99% chance the folder stays on the default home screen as well.
context: A Google partnerships VP tells colleagues how firm Google is on home screen placement terms in talks with Samsung.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0741, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Call between Patrick & Hiroshi
excerpt: -if Samsung threatens Wear, that's fine ... (call their bluff)... "it is disappointing" - "Maybe we need to reconsider our model for MADA" - "sounds like you can treat us transactionally on display, memory, SLSI, TV but you want us to do unnatural things for Mobile and give us zero credit for what we have contributed (and I mean zero)."
context: Draft talking points for a Google executive's call with a Samsung executive during contract talks.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0643, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Android OEM Revenue Share 3.0
excerpt: uh oh... Don: I think that somebody forgot to tell Anil that Sundar authorized the removal of Chrome from GMS a few months ago... How do you suggest we break the news? Oops, I included Anil on the thread! Anil: kidding aside, we never deviate from MADA obligations and Chrome distribution via GMS. No exceptions.
context: A joking exchange between Google Android and Chrome leaders about Chrome distribution rules for phone makers.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0608, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Sync on RU - question and heads-up
excerpt: also, is it possible to summarize what we are getting in the Xiaomi and Samsung RSA deals to show what gaps exist? i.e., in the new Samsung deal, we already get S-browser with Google default on a device by device basis. and as I mentioned earlier, I don't place much value on the Assistant icon on the home screen (primarily because it just confuses users and they have no idea what the difference is between search and Assistant).
context: A Google Android partnerships VP weighs which placements are worth paying phone makers for.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0809, published by the Department of Justice

subject: [Googlers] Business communications in a complicated world
excerpt: First, please write carefully and thoughtfully. We're an email and instant-messaging culture. We conduct much of our work online. We believe that information is good. But anything you write can become subject to review in legal discovery, misconstrued, or taken out of context, and may be used against you or us in ways you wouldn't expect.
context: A company-wide note from two senior Google leaders on how to write in email and chat while legal matters were pending.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX1101, published by the Department of Justice

subject: [Googlers] Business communications in a complicated world
excerpt: To help avoid inadvertent retention of instant messages, we have decided to make "off the record" the Google corporate default setting for Google Talk. We'll also be providing this option to our Google Apps enterprise customers.
context: The same 2008 note announced that Google Talk chats would no longer be saved by default.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX1101, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Really basic video ads questions
excerpt: Yes! Although no advertiser really says zero tolerance and we're still trying to seek out what an acceptable level is for many of the top brand advertisers.
context: A Google ads executive answers a question about how much unsafe content brand advertisers on YouTube will accept.

source.title: United States v. Google (search), trial exhibit UPX0342, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: sale reductions
excerpt: I was the hatchet man at DCLK back in 2000-2001 during the dotcom bust so have lived through this painful period before on display before. The biggest mistake made back then was the "death by a thousand cuts" scenario. That is, every quarter layoffs were made and the next quarter revenue shrank a bit more (because we didnt have the resources to keep the footprint in tact) and then more cuts were made until the business needed to be resurrected by a private equity firm.
context: Neal Mohan, then at DoubleClick inside Google, argues against deep cuts to the display ads business.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0041, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: sale reductions
excerpt: Fundamentally the glue that seals DFP to GCN is AdX (that is why it is the second pillar of our three-pillared strategy). It is essentially teh DFP - AdSense backfill we bought DCLK for but with the features that will actually get pubs to put their inventory into our ecosystem (dynamic allocation, competitive bidding from other networks, etc.).
context: Mohan explains why the AdX exchange ties Google's publisher ad server to its ad network.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0041, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: OpenX Market Launches!
excerpt: OpenX is the only relatively smaller player to offer the same three-pillared approach to the display market as us, Yahoo, MSFT and AOL - platform, exchange and network. Therefore I think we need to take them even more seriously than the other exchanges / yield managers that are gaining traction out there (Rubicon, etc.).
context: Neal Mohan sizes up a small rival ad exchange after its product launch.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0044, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: AdX TOS effectively prohibits publisher from using an adserver?
excerpt: This was a strategic decision. We allow redirection from 3rd party ad servers, but not from other exchanges or yield managers. Why? Because if we did then those systems would immediately have a super set of demand - anything the SSP had + all of AdX (including AdWords). No one would sign up for AdX directly.
context: A Google ad exchange product lead explains why AdX rules blocked rival exchanges from calling it.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0128, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Thanks - and we're asking the wrong question
excerpt: I would be remiss if I left CA without answering your question with an emphatic NO.
context: An employee gives a flat no when a Google executive asks whether to spin off DoubleClick.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0551, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: GOOGLE INTERNAL Copy of Q1 Programmatic OKR: margin manipulation investigation - Invitation to comment
excerpt: My take is that the main culprit is not dynamic revshare, but rather the fact that AdX gets last look over AppNexus (assuming AppNexus demand is booked as price priority LIs in DFP). AdX gets to pay high and win whenever AppNexus is present with a high CPM, and can pay low when AppNexus bids low.
context: A Google engineer describes how AdX could use a last look at rival bids, discussed after a rival's complaint.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0542, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Floors
excerpt: For #4 I'd say Bernanke in general. Any time we're willing to take negative revshare on a slice of traffic, we create an incentive for the pub to exploit that by setting a higher ask price.
context: A Google engineer comments on the pricing program known internally as Bernanke.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0609, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: Rubicon margins
excerpt: I think the other important thing to keep in mind versus most SSPs is that we also have the ad server. I think pure SSP is definitely commoditizing (and ultimately, I think only SSPs that also have an ad server will survive), but the combination is still more unique and not trivial to do well.
context: A Google ad tech leader explains why Google can charge more than rival ad exchanges.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0562, published by the Department of Justice

subject: GCP / DBM problem
excerpt: As you can see, things were largely on track through May; then went sideways in June & July, recovered partially in August and then started to slide more in September and kept getting worse, to the point where November is looking like -40% in spend YoY. I don't need to belabor the significance of this for us. How can you help here?
context: The CEO of rival exchange OpenX tells Google that spend from its DBM buying tool was falling sharply.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX1600, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Future of our margin on buyside and sellside
excerpt: I argued for many years that it is not justifiable to charge more for a simpler service which is sellside (just sort bids and declare the winner) and charge less for more expensive margin which is buyside.
context: A Google ads product leader questions the 20 percent AdX fee.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0737, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: TTD and Poirot
excerpt: I think we are maxed out on the "shift mix" strategy towards AdX. I'm also worried about erosion of the 20% AdX fee.
context: A Google ads leader worries about pressure on AdX fees while discussing how to price a new bidding feature.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0734, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: TTD
excerpt: It seems that TDD is spending 30% to 40% with Adx now whereas DBM is 75% with Adx. If TDD spend share on Adx drops further, it makes it harder to explain 75% DBM spend on Adx to external clients.
context: A Google ads leader on what a rival buying platform shifting spend away from AdX would mean for Google's own spend.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0897, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: OpenX lays off 100, more pressure on sellside take rates
excerpt: Are we comfortable telling the market that generally Google is comfortable with being 'non-transparent.'
context: A Google ad tech executive asks whether to disclose that the company keeps an undisclosed fee on some ad sales.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0719, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: "Source" advertising consortium
excerpt: My POV: When a buyer brings incremental demand in a network model - pubs don't seem to complain.
context: A Google ad tech executive on why publishers object to fees on Google's ad pipes and not on other buyers.

source.title: United States v. Google (ad tech), trial exhibit PTX0864, published by the Department of Justice

subject: Re: AWBID decision?
excerpt: the 6-9 month delay due to indecision is pure bullshit of course.
context: Neal Mohan, then a Google ads senior vice president, reacts to a long delay in a decision on the AdWords buying tool for the exchange.
